Author: @TheCommanderTaco
Content:
1. I wouldn't say this is "definitely way worse then the door kicking trend", but definitely had worse consequences and both are extremely dumb and terrible. This one for obvious reasons with sadly the state our world is in. Words a professor of mine once said have always stuck with me.

I wasn't around at the time, but was in my dorm room with my roommate when an announcement came on to make sure we didn't leave our rooms and had the doors locked. My roommate started getting worried that there might be a shooter, so we called one of his friends who did happen to be on campus. He did confirm the school was on lock down as the police were doing a sweep to make sure there was no danger. Apparently from what I heard an Atheist and Christian got into a argument. The Atheist left and came back later with a gun he shot into the air. Luckily that is all that happened. We were talking about it the following day in class and our professor was apparently working out in the gym when it happened. He was kinda deadpan. Not a strict person but also was stuck with classes having to teach people a subject they had no interest in since it was a core curriculum class. A student had asked him if he was scared and he turned and said "it's ridiculous to go out now in days and not expect a shooting to occur".  It saddens me to think like that, but having that in the back of your mind I also like to think it will help if such a situation is to ever arise. I always keep that possibility now in the back of my mind. Should a threat come out is there an escape route I can take or should I hope for the best.

Door one i think is worse because if the person doesn't have the money and / or materials needed to fix their door that is then both a physical and security risk to them.  Would make it easier for people to trespass into their property and steal.

Author: @nerdoftheatre
Content:
When I was in community college, I was headed to class. It's ten till and the hallways were a ghost town. I get grilled by an instructor, asking why I was in the hall. I said I left the bathroom and I'm headed to choir. 

I get thrown in the choir director's office. Apparently there was a threat to the HS. This was one month after an actual armed intruder injured a student at a HS an hour from us. 

We were under lockdown since we had HS students who often came to campus for class. All the schools in town got put on lockdown. 

The rest of the week, these threats kept happening. In total, 3 kids got slapped with felonies. This was before tiktok became big. 

There were HS students saying that the kids should've been let go. It was just a joke. We had federal organizations that showed up. 

I should reiterate. This was a month after a school nearby had a student injured due to an actual threat. (A teacher ended up jumping on the student and disarming him before any other damage could be done.)

How anyone can say, "It's just a joke." Sickens me.
